problem: The text says a notch "raises the local stress by Kf". Kf is the fatigue notch factor (a factor that reduces the endurance limit, Kf ≤ Kt). The local elastic stress is raised by the theoretical stress concentration factor Kt; Kf is not a stress raiser. A student would wrongly treat Kf as the stress concentration factor, which contradicts what Chapter 2.2 teaches.
fix: The notch raises the local stress by the theoretical stress concentration factor Kt (times the nominal stress). The fatigue notch factor Kf (Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1), q = notch sensitivity) is the smaller factor by which the fatigue strength or endurance limit is reduced, so the crack starts earlier at the notch.

problem: "Strength drops away from room temperature" suggests the endurance limit falls both above and below room temperature. In the standard Marin tables the drop is at elevated temperature; at low temperature kd is taken as 1 (static strength usually rises, though ductility falls).
fix: kd is the temperature factor. It is 1.0 at and below room temperature; the endurance limit falls as temperature rises well above room temperature (roughly above 200–250 °C for steel).

problem: The second series draws S = 230 MPa across the whole range 10³ to 10⁷, but the curve itself is flat only after 10⁶ cycles. The overlay duplicates the flat part of the S–N series and makes the endurance limit look like a limit from 10³ cycles onward.
fix: Draw the Se reference line only from 10⁶ to 10⁷ (or keep it as a faint level line labelled clearly as a level, not as part of the curve), so the slope ends exactly at the knee.

problem: "A slope of −0.12 per decade is not −0.12 per cycle" is confusing: b is the slope of log₁₀ S against log₁₀ N, so 3 decades means 3b in log S. The phrase does not tell the student what to do differently.
fix: Use log₁₀ consistently: b = Δlog₁₀S / Δlog₁₀N, so over 3 decades log₁₀S changes by 3b. Do not mix log₁₀ with ln, and do not read b as a change in S per cycle.

problem: "A larger section has less support from the core" is vague and does not say why kb falls.
fix: In a larger section the stress gradient is flatter and a bigger volume of material is highly stressed, so a weak spot is more likely; kb therefore falls as the diameter rises.

problem: "Chapter 2.2" and "Chapter 2.4" are written as plain text, so on a phone the student cannot jump to them.
fix: Make them chapter links in the series format, for example Chapter 2.2 and Chapter 2.4 (use the actual chapter ids).
